```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(igraph)
```

```{r}
bac = read_csv("Results/bac_otu_genus_glom.csv")
fun = read_csv("Results/fun_otu_genus_glom.csv")
```

```{r}
both = fun %>% left_join(bac, by = "DO_ID") %>% # left join because fewer samples have fungal rna data than bacterial
  select(-c(...1.x, barcodes.x, ...1.y, barcodes.y)) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "DO_ID")

# am I loosing primary lifestyle here?
```


```{r}
# calculate correlation matrix
cor_matrix = cor(both, method = "spearman")

# Set a threshold (e.g., correlations > 0.6 are edges)
cor_matrix[abs(cor_matrix) < 0.6] <- 0
```


```{r}
net <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edge_list, directed = FALSE)

# You can now color nodes based on Kingdom
V(net)$kingdom <- ifelse(V(net)$name %in% taxa_names(ps_bacteria), "Bacteria", "Fungi")
plot(net, vertex.color = as.factor(V(net)$kingdom))
```
